findings.title: English reference path derivation is fragile and can point to the wrong file
findings.body: The English counterpart is derived by string-replacing 'resources-community' with 'resources' and then regex-replacing any '_xx.properties' suffix with '_en.properties' across the whole absolute path. Any directory containing an underscore or matching the regex (for example a checkout path like /home/user/my_project/...) gets mangled, and the first replaceAll on 'resources-community' can also affect unrelated path segments. If the English file is missing, the verifier throws a RuntimeException, failing the whole build rather than reporting a message.

findings.title: verifySafeHtml runs on the English source file itself and on files with no English counterpart
findings.body: verify() calls verifySafeHtml() for every properties file, including *_en.properties. For the English file the reference is itself, which is fine, but for files whose key is absent in English the fallback is an empty string, so any HTML in a translated-only key is flagged as illegal without any source to compare to. Also the code calls the file-based bundle reader twice per file, and an IOException on the English file is converted to an unchecked RuntimeException instead of a MojoExecutionException, inconsistent with verify()'s error contract.

findings.title: Anchor-tag check reports error but sanitization continues and can produce misleading diffs
findings.body: santizeAnchors adds a message and breaks on the first unmatched anchor, but the value is still passed through the sanitizer and a second 'Illegal HTML' message can be emitted for the same key. Also replaceFirst with Pattern.quote removes the first occurrence in the value regardless of position, so a translation whose anchors are in a different order than the source can pass or fail for the wrong reason.

findings.title: Substring computation can throw when diff indices overlap
findings.body: The start/end prefix and suffix trimming is computed independently, so when value and sanitized are identical in a region that overlaps (e.g. one string is a prefix/suffix repetition of the other), start can exceed value.length() - end. Then value.substring(start, value.length() - end) throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, crashing the verifier for that file instead of reporting the problem.

findings.title: Plugin now depends on owasp sanitizer and commons-text at compile scope without version alignment
findings.body: commons-text and owasp-java-html-sanitizer are added as runtime dependencies of a Maven plugin, so every consumer of the plugin pulls them in transitively. commons-text 1.13.0 also pulls commons-lang3 and the sanitizer version is pinned separately; no dependency management or justification is given for these versions.

findings.title: Tests use hasItem instead of exact-match assertions and the positive path is untested
findings.body:
The tests were weakened from contains(...) to hasItem(...) and only check that some message matches a substring. There is no test that a clean translation produces zero messages, so false positives from the sanitizer on legitimate content (e.g.
or {0} placeholders) would go undetected. The noHtml_de test also uses a fixture key that is identical in structure to the illegal case, so it does not verify the allowed-tag path.

findings.title: Fixture is named as the English file but the test only checks itself for illegal HTML
findings.body: illegalHtmlTag_en.properties has an unclosed <div> and is verified against itself as the English reference, so the test is really exercising the English-file path rather than a translation. The test name suggests it covers translations; the fixture does not cover the translated-vs-source comparison at all.

findings.title: Finnish totpStep1 replaced with a key whose wording no longer names the apps, and other locales copy the same change
findings.body: Multiple locales (fi, sv, sk, zh_CN, lt in the account bundle, and login bundles) had the link-bearing totpStep1 text replaced by a generic sentence. The Lithuanian account change (messages_lt.properties line 101) replaces the translation with Italian text ('Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'), which is a clearly wrong-language string shipped to Lithuanian users.

findings.title: Lithuanian translation replaced with Italian text
findings.body: The totpStep1 value in the Lithuanian account messages is replaced with 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:', which is Italian. Lithuanian users will see untranslated Italian text in the TOTP setup page. The same Italian string also appears in messages_lt.properties of the login bundle and in the Lithuanian login messages (loginTotpStep1) and the account messages for zh_CN and other locales, indicating an accidental copy from another locale.

findings.title: Hungarian emailUpdateConfirmationBodyHtml has a stray *** prefix
findings.body: The line emailUpdateConfirmationBodyHtml begins with '***' in the diff, which becomes part of the key name and makes the property key '***emailUpdateConfirmationBodyHtml'. The real key is therefore missing from the bundle and the HTML body falls back to the default/English value or fails to render.

findings.title: Lithuanian email HTML links changed to malformed attribute syntax
findings.body: The change replaces unquoted href=LT"..." with href="..." for several keys, which is a correction, but the same diff also leaves 'nJei' and other typos. More importantly the diff is unrelated to the sanitizer; combined with the Italian totpStep1 change in other files this suggests unreviewed bulk edits.

findings.title: Dutch emailVerificationBodyHtml closing tag typo introduced
findings.body: The change to emailVerificationBodyHtml adds a closing tag, but the diff shows the original '' malformed fragment was reshaped; the final result is correct only if the fix is applied as shown. Given the verifier now flags malformed HTML, the corrected string should be checked against the sanitizer, otherwise the build check introduced by this PR fails on this locale.

findings.title: Norwegian identityProviderLinkBody drops HTML from plain-text template
findings.body: The identityProviderLinkBody (plain text) was changed to contain no <b> tags but the diff also modifies the HTML-producing template in the Norwegian bundle. Changing plain-text bodies to remove HTML that was placeholder-adjacent may be intended, but the change is applied to a body that the verifier only treats as HTML-free, so the change is not needed for the sanitizer and alters the email content without justification.

findings.title: Slovak error-invalid-multivalued-size placeholder fix changes wrong argument
findings.body: The corrected pattern changes {1,choice,...} to {2,choice,...} for the max count, which is correct, but the key is placed at the end of a file that previously lacked a trailing newline and the choice format 4<hodnôt is used for both min and max, so the plural form for values above 4 is still mishandled for the minimum part. Plural forms are not verified against the English source.

findings.title: Czech multivalued-size message uses min choice on wrong argument
findings.body: The new error-invalid-multivalued-size line in Czech uses {1,choice,...} for the minimum and {2,choice,...} for the maximum, which matches the English pattern. However the Czech line is appended after readOnlyUsernameMessage without a preceding blank line, and the same key is also present in the English source with a different plural structure, so translators' plural rules are unverified.

findings.title: Duplicate error-invalid-multivalued-size key in login bundle
findings.body: The login messages_en.properties now contains error-invalid-multivalued-size with the new choice syntax, and the admin bundle contains the same key. Keys shared between bundles with differing choice syntax can drift; the verifier only checks sanitizer rules, not cross-bundle consistency.

findings.title: Changed English message format string to ChoiceFormat without escaping the choice literal
findings.body: The new error-invalid-multivalued-size value uses '{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}' and the original used '{{2}}' double-brace syntax. The account UI is i18next-based, which interpolates with {{ }} and does not use java MessageFormat choice syntax, so the placeholders {0}, {1}, {2} are not substituted and the choice text is shown literally to users.
